mem.10:
27 Mar 2023: Audrey and Andrew caught up. Andrew had started a Financial Analyst job the previous week. Audrey said she had three dogs—Pepper, Precious and Panda—and had had them for three years. She adored them, had recently bought collars and tags, and took them to parks and trails. She shared a photo of two collared dogs on grass. Andrew had no pets but loved animals, especially birds and eagles; he shared a photo of two birds flying against the sun. He recommended the scenic Fox Hollow trail for a weekend; Audrey planned to try it.

2 Apr 2023: Audrey’s household adopted Pixie, a small white puppy, bringing the pack to four dogs. Pixie settled in after a few days; Pepper initially needed time, but they grew close. Andrew was considering a dog but had trouble finding dog-friendly city housing. Audrey recommended pet-friendly housing search filters her household had used; Andrew planned to try them. They discussed dogs as companions and hiking partners. Andrew missed exploring trails with his family dog and shared photos of a man walking a dog on a trail and a man sitting on a rock with a dog. He said hiking with a dog was fun and built bonds and memories. Audrey wanted to hike with her dogs.

8–9 Apr 2023: Andrew and his girlfriend visited a city café after a long week and enjoyed coffee and pastries (croissants, muffins, tarts). He shared a bakery display photo.

16 Apr 2023: Andrew missed nature and hiking. Outdoors made him feel at home, connected, restored and refreshed his mind with a different outlook; he turned to nature for a reset, though city life made getting outside hard. Audrey said walks with her dogs grounded and recharged her. They planned a pastry party; Audrey shared a blueberry muffin and dog photos, saying the dogs would come. She couldn’t imagine life without them. Her arm tattoo depicts a dog and sunflowers, representing love of dogs and nature and wanting to see their faces even when apart.

Week of 24–30 Apr 2023: Audrey hiked and saw a hummingbird darting with wings spread; later shared a photo.

3 May 2023: Andrew found nearby open space and tried to hike outside the city every weekend. Nature felt therapeutic, peaceful, refreshing and invigorating; he liked greenery, mountain views and fresh air. He shared sunset lake/mountain and mountain-range photos to share peaceful moments and encourage positivity. Audrey was busy with pets; her dogs loved hiking, scents, fetch (ball/frisbee), playdates, toys, treats and party hats. She used leashes/shoes for safety. She recommended a wooded dog park with benches near their usual park; Andrew planned to visit.

6 May 2023: Andrew continued seeking a dog through websites, shelters and friends; it was fun but frustrating. He shared a dog-at-shelter photo. He thought a smaller dog suited apartment life and advised considering space and breed exercise needs. He sought pet-friendly housing near a park/woods, contacted landlords and checked neighborhoods, wanting open space for a dog and proximity to nature. Audrey lived near a park; the previous Friday she took her dogs on a road trip to a national park, where they ran in a field. She takes them on road trips every couple of months; Andrew added one to his bucket list. Audrey offered help and wanted a photo of his future dog; he was visiting another shelter and promised updates.

11 May 2023: Andrew hiked with friends and girlfriend the previous weekend at his new spot; shared a dirt path to a grassy hill. Audrey said she had four dogs and spent much of her free time caring for them and keeping them happy and healthy. She had enrolled in a positive-reinforcement pet-bonding workshop for the following month. She shared a dog group photo and a friendly store volunteer’s dog. She expected her quick-learning, reward-loving dogs to do well and promised updates/tips. Both opposed punishment; Audrey said hurting her dogs pained her. Andrew would explore positive-reinforcement classes.

1–2 Jun 2023: Audrey’s dogs ran and played off-leash at a park; their happiness brought her joy and peace. Andrew shared a sunset mountain photo with a grazing horse and asked about her hike. Audrey said the previous week she’d hiked with the dogs to a national-park peak at sunset; they ran around in a breeze and birdsong. She shared a photo of two horses in a fenced field. Nature cheered her and made her grateful. Andrew still couldn’t find pet-friendly city housing but remained determined. Audrey offered to help search if he emailed his criteria.

13 Jun 2023: Andrew took a rock-climbing class with friends the previous Sunday, reached the top and shared summit-view and climber photos. It was challenging and satisfying; friends’ cheers helped. Nature pushed him outside his comfort zone, and he planned more activities, including kayaking and possibly bungee jumping. During the week before this date, Audrey found a small park with a tree-surrounded trail where she walked her dogs and invited Andrew to join; he accepted. Her dogs enjoyed meeting people. She shared photos of them playing ball/frisbee in a meadow. Walks lasted about an hour at the dogs’ pace; exploring and exercise left them smiling and tired. Their faces brightened when she prepared for their favorite part of the day. Audrey’s happy place was outdoors with her dogs; both found nature peaceful, inspiring, refreshing and centering.

26 Jun 2023: Audrey had moved to a new home with a bigger backyard; she shared a photo of two dogs on the grass in front of the house. Her four dogs loved running and sniffing around; she made a backyard play area with agility equipment and toys. Andrew shared a photo of dogs playing indoors at a nearby doggy daycare, which Audrey planned to check out. They agreed pets bring joy and are family; Audrey couldn’t understand people who hate or hurt them. Andrew shared a colorful flower-bed photo from his neighborhood park. Audrey was unpacking. Andrew had hiked with friends the previous Friday in good weather; he enjoyed birdsong, tree scents and outdoors, missed nature’s peace, and had not yet reviewed photos. Audrey shared photos of feet on a rock overlooking a lake and someone seated on the rock, recalling a hike years earlier with friends when they found a beautiful mountain lake and sat chatting and admiring the view. Both called it calming and valued life’s small things and not taking anything for granted.

3 Jul 2023: Audrey was taking a challenging but rewarding dog-training course; her dogs were already doing better. She and Andrew had little time for new trails; Andrew still couldn’t find dog-friendly rentals and was limited to urban adventures. Audrey said nature with her dogs was calming and restorative and shared a photo of two dogs running in a field with a ball. Her four dogs were all mutts: two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes. They loved running and fetch. She shared photos of two dogs curled in a dog bed and two on a couch under a blanket. All four were three years old and a great pack. They’d had a fun, somewhat chaotic doggy playdate the previous Friday. Audrey called the dogs her universe.

Andrew had been exploring cooking since he couldn’t hike; it helped him de-stress and be creative, though he was a rookie. Audrey loved cooking, experimenting with recipes as an escape and creative outlet. Her favorite recipe was family chicken pot pie, a longstanding recipe that reminded her of her grandmother’s kitchen and conversations at the table; she offered to send it and shared pie photos (including lattice top). Audrey liked cooking with music and a glass of wine and found it therapeutic/self-care. Garlic was her go-to ingredient. She offered Andrew her roasted chicken recipe and shared a pan-of-chicken-and-potatoes photo. It was based on Mediterranean flavors and used chicken, garlic, lemon and herbs; it was easy, healthy and her favorite comfort meal. Andrew was keen to try it and promised to report back.

11 Jul: Andrew introduced Toby, a new puppy, despite city living; he shared an indoor leash photo. Work piled up and he missed hiking; Audrey suggested hiking together. 4 Aug: Andrew, his girlfriend and Toby planned weekend camping; he shared a photo of a woman setting up a tent on a rocky hill. Audrey started agility classes with her dogs at a park, practicing twice weekly; they learned, bonded and overcame challenges. They exchanged dog/trail photos. Andrew planned a small local-trail hike with Toby.

16 Aug: Audrey got another arm tattoo depicting her four dogs; they meant so much that she wanted to carry them wherever she went. She shared a tattoo photo. A vet trip with all four was chaotic; next time she’d go one at a time. Favorite resting spots: Pepper—couch; Pixie—bed; Precious—chair; Panda—rug. Andrew shared Toby on his fluffy blanket; Audrey shared two dogs on their favorite couch blanket. All four dogs cuddled during naps and were best friends. Seeing them together made Audrey happy; she couldn’t imagine life without them. Andrew agreed pets were family and shared himself on the couch with Toby.

24 Aug: Andrew and his girlfriend went fishing at a nearby lake the previous weekend, caught a few fish and had fun. Audrey had never fished, but had relaxed by lakes. She recalled a peaceful mountain-lake trip with friends years earlier—birds, still water, fresh air—and shared a photo of dogs on a rock by a lake. Andrew asked how her dogs stayed good-looking outdoors; Audrey said daily brushing, regular baths, nail trims and love. Caring for them was serious responsibility, sometimes tough but rewarding; she wanted them happy. Andrew

Andrew and girlfriend got Scout a bed, toys and puppy pads as a safe, comfortable space. Audrey advised slow introductions to Toby and Buddy. Andrew shared neighborhood flowers and said he’d hiked the prior Friday; Audrey recalled a beautiful mountain-lake hike with friends years earlier.

3–27 Jul: Audrey’s challenging dog-training course was rewarding; her four 3-year-old mutts—two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes—were improving. They love running, fetch and playdates; Audrey called them her universe. Andrew still couldn’t find dog-friendly rentals. He took up cooking to de-stress; Audrey also finds it calming. Her family-recipe chicken pot pie evokes her grandma and kitchen conversations; she promised the recipe. She likes music, wine and improvising, often uses garlic, and offered a Mediterranean roasted chicken recipe (chicken, garlic, lemon, herbs). Andrew and girlfriend picnicked; Audrey suggested a hike together next month and they agreed, discussing off-leash safety. Andrew adopted German Shepherd puppy Toby on 11 Jul despite city living; work kept him indoors and he missed hiking. Audrey makes personalized wooden dog tags/keychains. Andrew, girlfriend and Toby volunteered at a shelter on a Monday before 27 Jul; Andrew said animal volunteering was his way to give back and improve animals’ lives. Audrey might volunteer someday and shared a photo kissing a dog at a park. Audrey described her dogs: oldest a relaxed “wise old sage,” second playful, third naughty but cuddly, youngest adventurous. Childhood dog Max was energetic and loved fetch; Audrey recalled neighborhood walks and confiding hopes and worries to him. They discussed pets as confidantes, unconditional love and lasting memories.

4–24 Aug: Andrew, girlfriend and Toby camped; a shared photo showed a woman setting up a tent on a rocky hill. Audrey began agility classes with her pups at the dog park, practicing twice weekly; fun, challenging, good exercise and bonding. Shared photos showed dogs/field, ring jump, group dogs and trail hike; the hike took two hours with great views. Andrew’s favorite outdoor activity is hiking; reaching a hard summit makes worries vanish. He hopes for a deep bond with smart, loyal Toby and wants city life not to limit him. Audrey said shepherds enjoy exploring and need time, attention, walks and exercise; Andrew planned a local-trail hike with Toby. Audrey got an arm tattoo of her four dogs and may get more dogs someday, but four are enough for now. On 16 Aug she took all four to the vet; it was chaotic, so next time she’d go one by one. Favorite spots: Pepper on couch, Pixie on bed, Precious on chair, Panda on rug; Toby likes a fluffy floor blanket. Audrey’s dogs cuddle and are best friends. Andrew and girlfriend visited a farm for fresh vegetables. On 19 Aug Andrew took a work break at a cafe and shared a serene sunset-over-mountain-with-church hiking photo. Audrey learned to groom her pups: go slowly and gently, watch ears/paws, be patient and positive. Andrew planned a nature-reserve visit. On 24 Aug Andrew and girlfriend went fishing at a nearby lake, caught a few fish and enjoyed it. Audrey had never fished but likes relaxing by lakes and recalled a peaceful mountain lake with birds and still water; she shared a photo of dogs on a rock by a lake. Her care routine includes daily brushing, regular baths, nail trims and lots of love. Toby photos showed him asleep in a dog bed and sitting with a leash.

6 Sep: Andrew said work was stressful and crowded out outdoor activities; Audrey encouraged self-care and aims for at least one self-care activity daily. Andrew added morning coffee and lunchtime walks. Audrey organized a neighborhood dog playdate (photo of two dogs playing in a fenced area) and bought new beds for cooler weather (photo of dog on bed). Andrew hiked the prior weekend and shared a person on a mountain overlooking the city at sunset. He wants Toby to hike but Toby is too young. Andrew was still struggling to find dog-friendly housing; Audrey encouraged him.

24 Sep: Audrey said a pup (Andrew thought Precious) saw something at the park the previous Friday and pulled so hard the leash broke; Audrey chased and caught her safely. Shared photo of red retractable leash with black handle. Audrey calmed the dog with petting, hugs, calm speech and a slow walk; she shared a dog resting on a bed with head on pillow. Andrew wants a similarly strong bond with Toby. Audrey advised patience, regular training, time, love and praise. They train obedience and tricks: sit, stay, shake and roll over. Audrey walks the dogs multiple times daily; they are all mutts, two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes. Shared photos included dogs in birthday hats, sitting together, playing, and snuggling. Audrey has a small garden and veggie patch; gardening relaxes her and feels accomplishing. She grows Peruvian Lilies, which are easy to care for with water and sun. The dogs enjoy exploring and running in the garden; they play only with her own dogs. Audrey says they bring joy, love and happiness and mean everything to her. Andrew shared a balcony flower photo.
mem.28:
27 Mar 2023: Audrey and Andrew reconnected. Andrew had recently started a Financial Analyst job, loved animals, eagles and hiking, had no pets then, and struggled to find pet-friendly housing. Audrey had four dogs—Pepper, Precious, Panda and Pixie—hiked with them, recommended Fox Hollow and offered housing help.

Apr 2023: Pixie, a new puppy, settled in over a few days and bonded with Pepper. Andrew missed hiking with his family dog; they shared dog-trail photos and agreed hikes make lasting memories. 16 Apr Audrey shared photos of dogs running and a woman walking dogs in woods. During the week of 24–30 Apr, she saw a hummingbird darting around with wings spread.

Apr–Jun 2023: Audrey shared café, coffee and pastry photos and suggested a pastry party with her dogs. Her tattoos include dogs and sunflowers. She prioritizes leashes, footwear and safety on hikes and uses positive reinforcement. In May she road-tripped with her dogs to a national park; Andrew added a dog road trip to his bucket list. Audrey hiked with them to a peak at sunset; her favorite photo showed two horses in a field. Andrew hiked with friends/girlfriend, took a rock-climbing class, and wanted more outdoor activities (kayaking, possibly bungee jumping). Audrey invited him to walk her dogs; they enjoy people, fetch, frisbee and walks. Andrew mentioned dog daycare. On 2 Jun Audrey offered to help him find suitable dog-friendly housing and asked him to email his criteria. By 26 Jun she had moved to a house with a bigger yard, agility equipment and toys. Both consider pets family and oppose cruelty. They agreed to hike together with Audrey’s dogs in August when weather was more pleasant; Andrew suggested a trail and shared its map, Audrey planned to look into it. They hoped the dogs could run freely, while keeping safety in mind.

Jul–Aug 2023: Audrey’s challenging dog-training course was rewarding; her four 3-year-old mutts improved. They love running, fetch and playdates; she calls them her universe. She promised her grandmother’s chicken pot-pie recipe; likes music, wine, improvising and garlic, and offered Mediterranean roasted chicken. Andrew adopted German Shepherd Toby on 11 Jul; work kept him indoors and he missed hiking. He and girlfriend volunteered at a shelter. Audrey makes personalized wooden dog tags/keychains. Dog personalities: oldest relaxed/wise, second playful, third naughty/cuddly, youngest adventurous. Childhood dog Max loved fetch and was her confidant. Andrew, girlfriend and Toby camped. Audrey began agility twice weekly, shared dog/ring-jump photos and a two-hour hike. Andrew loves summits, where worries vanish. Audrey tattooed four dogs on her arm; four are enough for now. 16 Aug: vet trip with all four was chaotic; next time one at a time. Sleeping spots: Pepper couch, Pixie bed, Precious chair, Panda rug; Toby fluffy floor blanket. Audrey learned gentle grooming, brushes daily and bathes/trims nails regularly. Andrew and girlfriend visited a vegetable farm and fished at a lake; Audrey likes peaceful lakes but has never fished. She had a fun outdoor day with her dogs and said she’d always cherish those moments. Andrew planned a nature-reserve visit/photos for Audrey around 19–20 Aug.

Sep 2023: Work stress kept Andrew from outdoors; Audrey encouraged self-care and one activity daily. On 6 Sep she said she makes time for at least one daily self-care activity, e.g. treating herself. Andrew added morning coffee and lunch walks. Audrey arranged dog playdate, bought beds for cool weather and recommended dog parks. Andrew hiked and hoped Toby could hike when older; housing search was hard. 24 Sep: a dog (Andrew guessed Precious) pulled so hard Audrey’s leash broke; she caught and soothed her. Audrey advised patience, training, love and praise. Dogs know sit/stay/shake/roll over; she walks them several times daily and they explore her garden/vegetable patch. She grows easy-care Peruvian lilies.

Oct 2023: Andrew and girlfriend planned a November beach trip with Toby; shared ocean sunset. Audrey shared dogs at shaded dog park. They discussed birdwatching; Audrey wants to try, Andrew offered to go and log birds. Both value nature and protecting ecosystems. Audrey recycles; Andrew suggested biking/transit and river routes. 4 Oct: dogs enjoyed beach swimming/play. Andrew felt a “void in his heart” from city/work-life imbalance; Audrey suggested houseplants/weekend parks. After Audrey injured her knee and recovered, she shared dogs running in a field. She makes jewelry from recycled bottle caps/buttons/broken jewelry, sells it and donates some proceeds to an animal shelter. 13 Oct: Andrew, girlfriend and Toby had board-game night; Audrey baked neighbor thank-you treats. Andrew planned café visit and coffee by dog park; Audrey agreed to bring pups. Toby loves sweaters, is active and once chased a squirrel around a tree. Audrey’s dogs like fetch/frisbee/running/meeting dogs, dislike snow and prefer sun. She added drawings to her four-dog tattoo. Andrew misses nature and seeks parks/hikes; Audrey sees hikes as therapy. 19 Oct Andrew adopted shelter puppy Buddy, who was settling in and adjusting to Toby; Buddy likes walks, fresh air and trails. Andrew enjoys walks with Buddy, who likes exploring new trails with him and others. Audrey offered to find a trail like his photo of a remote dirt road with a cow and red truck. 24 Oct: Andrew/girlfriend enjoyed wine tasting. Audrey had an accident playing with dogs and a cast on her arm, but was improving. Andrew tried sushi for the first time; Audrey loves it and recommended California or salmon rolls and dipping sauces. He promised photos. Andrew said his girlfriend and he had a picnic date planned for Sunday 29 Oct.

28 Oct 2023: Audrey said dogs had been acting abnormally; she saw an animal behaviorist the previous Wednesday. The appointment went okay: questions, handling tips and routine changes. Positive reinforcement was helping; dogs showed progress, though it would take time. Shared summer photo of two dogs running with a ball. All are mutts: Pepper/Panda Lab mixes; Precious/Pixie Chihuahua mixes (earlier she described two Jack Russell and two Chihuahua mixes). Andrew shared a national-park mountain-hiking photo. They planned a dog-friendly Saturday hike by a lake with views; Andrew said it was nearby and shared trail photos; Audrey would bring snacks. They hoped for a future autumn-color trip and dog photos. Both valued their friendship and shared love of nature/dogs. Andrew shared dog-in-park, dog-eating-from-bowl and himself-with-dog-on-trail photos. Audrey admired the happy dog and they anticipated an “epic and fun hike.” Earlier, they had also planned to hike together in August.

4 Nov 2023: Andrew and girlfriend biked to a park outside town. Audrey had joined a weekly dog owners’ group for tips and dog play. Andrew considered a third dog but worried Toby and Buddy were already a lot; Audrey advised focusing on their happiness and health. She said city dog ownership is tough but doable with daily exercise, socialization and mental stimulation. She shared toy/fetch/frisbee photos and uses puzzles, training and hide-and-seek. Andrew planned to try enrichment with his dogs. They expressed gratitude and affection; Audrey said their friendship means a lot and “that’s what friends are for.”

22 Nov 2023: Audrey said her four dogs went to a pet salon the previous Friday, were excited and looked cute and shiny afterward; they behaved well in the unfamiliar place. She shared a groomed-dog photo and joked she was a good dog mom. Andrew had not yet taken his dogs to a groomer; he has long been interested in learning grooming but hasn’t had time. He said he had adopted another dog, Scout, and shared a photo of a woman feeding a dog hay in a barn. He and his girlfriend planned a small nearby-park outing with Scout, Toby and Buddy, keeping Scout leashed and gradually introducing the dogs. They had gotten Scout a bed, toys and puppy
